How to use

  • Diffuse 3 drops with cypress or cedarwood.
  • Dilute to 2% for a body oil after exercise.
  • Add 3 drops to a bath with epsom salts.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Pine resin
  • Green berry
  • Cold air

What's in it

  • 100% pure Juniperus communis berry oil

Who it's for

People who like resinous scents

Crisp and piney, and a natural partner for cedarwood and cypress.

Post-exercise blends

Common in body oils after exertion, usually at 2% in a carrier.

Gin drinkers

Instantly recognisable, though drier and more resinous than the spirit.

What people get wrong

Buying juniper berry and getting juniper wood or needle oil. They are distilled from different parts of the same tree, smell different and are priced differently. Check what the label says.

Using it in pregnancy. Juniper appears on most avoid lists.

What it won't do

We make no claims about what it does. It is a clean, resinous scent that many people like after exercise, and that is as far as we will go.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Juniper Berry

Is this the same juniper used in gin?

Same species, Juniperus communis, and the same berries. The oil is more concentrated and drier than the spirit, where the juniper is one botanical among many.

What is the difference between berry and needle oil?

Berry oil is softer and fruitier; needle and wood oils are sharper and more turpentine-like, and considerably cheaper. Suppliers do not always distinguish them clearly.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. Avoid during pregnancy. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.
